title: Candidate fit digest (scratch) — Mikael Rhee
content:
Quick scratchpad after loop with candidate (L) for Senior Runtime Engineer role. Purpose: capture raw impressions, hypotheses, and a lightweight scorecard to decide whether to move to an extended take-home or hire loop. This is messy — notes to self and to hiring panel.

Context / interview runbook references:
- interview loop: phone screen (Anu), systems deep-dive (me), runtime pairing (Diego), culture + mgmt (Priya)
- rubric: confluence:INFRT-245 (link in artifacts)
- job posting: senior-runtime-eng (s-re)

High-level impression (one-liner):
- Strong systems intuition and edge-case thinking, shaky on quantization/low-level CUDA details and some modern batching tradeoffs. Communicates clearly, pragmatic about incremental fixes. Slight risk on scaling to multi-tenant production without senior mentorship.

Raw notes by segment:
1) Systems / architecture (45m)
- Walked through how they would re-architect a single-GPU serving worker that needs to support both 8k and 32k contexts.
- L sketched sharding-by-request-size idea + multi-queue priority system. Good on backpressure and isolation (per-queue token budgets).
- Missed KV-cache invalidation race scenarios initially; after prompt, proposed a lease/token approach (ok).
- Brought up preemption for long queries, aware of fairness vs SLOs tradeoffs.
- Weakness: when pressed on memory layout for attention cache and end-to-end throughput implications, answers were handwavy — used high-level terms (packed buffers) but couldn't outline simple pointer-level plan or estimate memory overhead precisely.

2) Inference implementation / perf (30m)
- Familiar with batching concepts and pointers to kernel-level optimization examples (Winograd not relevant but demonstrates breadth).
- Limited practical experience with quantization toolchains (no hands-on with q8/q4 ops or Triton kernels). Has read papers (GPTQ, LLM.int8()) but hasn't shipped quantized pipelines before.
- Good intuition for IO-bound vs compute-bound breakdown; suggested layered microbenchmarks to characterize hotspots.

3) Pairing / troubleshooting (40m)
- Pair task: debug simple memory leak in a toy runtime loop. L found the leak within ~15m, identified root cause (missing cache free on early-exit), wrote a clean test case. Shows solid debugging practices and test-first mindset.
- When asked to make a small perf improvement, proposed micro-batching with dynamic cutoff heuristics; code skeleton ok but missed one off-by-one that would break edge case — not a dealbreaker for senior hire but flag for review discipline.

4) Communication & culture (20m)
- Very transparent about limits: said they "haven't shipped quantized inference yet" but motivated to learn.
- Positive on blameless postmortems, emphasized observability (traces + token-level metrics).
- Good at simplifying complex tradeoffs for PM/infra audiences.

Behavioral / leadership signals:
- Has led a small infra team (3 engineers) for 18 months — experience with oncall rotations and incident playbooks.
- Described a time they pushed back on an exec roadmap to protect SLOs (reasonable diplomatic framing).
- Not a strong org-builder resume (no hiring plan sketch), but could be a solid IC+ mentor.

Scorecard (0-5 scale, quick):
- Deep systems design: 4
- Low-level inference / quantization: 2
- Debugging & code hygiene: 4
- Production scalability (multi-tenant): 3
- Communication / cross-team: 4
- Leadership / ownership: 3
Overall quick average: 3.3 -> leaning towards move-to-take-home (focused) rather than direct hire.

Risk flags (things to validate if we move forward):
- Lack of hands-on quantization experience — our Dedicated and Private customers will expect this competency quickly. Need to confirm learning curve and commitment.
- Edge-case correctness discipline — small off-by-one in pairing task; check for propensity to rush. Pairing was good but add a static analysis or testing checklist during next round.
- Not much experience with HSM/KMS integrations (relevant for Private deployments).

Suggested tailored take-home / next step (short):
- Small focused take-home: "Quant-aware inference microservice" (3–6 hours expected). Goals: implement a tiny Python/C++ wrapper or Triton-like mock that demonstrates integration of a simulated quantized op (we provide the stub), implement dynamic batching logic, and add a microbenchmark + a unit test that verifies KV-cache eviction under race. Deliverables: short writeup (design choices + perf numbers). This will directly validate the two main gaps: quantization practical knowledge and production correctness discipline.

Interview ask / questions for panel calibration:
- How much weight do we give lack of quantization hands-on? If we hire, can we pair them with an applied-ml engineer for first 3 months?
- If we require quantization shipped before start, likely no; but if ask is learning-in-role with product support + onboarding plan, they might be a good match.

Logistics / recommended routing: 
- Recommend: invite for curated take-home. If take-home looks acceptable, bring back for a focused follow-up (45m) on quant deployment patterns + a short system-architecture deep dive.
- Interviewer notes to include with homework: check for correctness edge cases in tests, and confirm they can reproduce microbench numbers locally.

Staging notes to include in candidate card (for ATS / GH ticket):
- Quick summary for hiring packet (1–2 lines): "Strong systems senior IC with excellent debugging and product sense; limited hands-on quantization work — recommend targeted take-home to validate low-level inference shipping readiness."
- Suggested compensation band thoughts: senior IC (leveling match depends on quantization outcome).

Open questions / TODO for my follow-ups: 
- Draft take-home description + test harness (Diego + me).
- Slack DM to Anu/Diego to sync on interview fragmentation and add pairing testcase.
- Add candidate to candidate tracker: hiring/candidates/2025-Q4 (Jira ticket INFR-487).

Links / artifacts referenced: confluence:INFRT-245 (rubric), jira:INFR-487, github:repo/pr/1123 (pairing harness), slack:GB9ABC/thread-xyz

Notes to self: keep this short in panel summary — the risk is fixable with an oriented 6–8 week onboarding + mentor. Candidate seems coachable and pragmatic.

End of scratchpad.
recommended_next_steps: Assign Diego + me to draft a 3-6 hour take-home focused on quant/eviction correctness. Send Slack ping to Anu to align. Move candidate to take-home stage if they accept.
scorecard_summary: Average 3.3; good systems intuition and debugging; missing quantization hands-on; proceed with targeted homework to validate low-level inference readiness.
